faq.q: How is my monthly fee set?
faq.a: A review of your site, competitors and goals informs a fixed written quote. The appropriate plan depends on the work your market needs.

faq.q: Which language should our pages use?
faq.a: We look at how your customers search, then plan English, Urdu or Roman Urdu content to suit those searches.

faq.q: What access helps you get started?
faq.a: Website access and existing Search Console and Analytics accounts are useful. We can help set up measurement when those accounts are missing.

deliverables: Essentials — keyword planning, on-page work for up to ten priority pages and technical checks.
Growth — four new pages or guides per month, coverage for up to three cities and digital PR.
Custom — a scoped plan for e-commerce, larger sites or multiple brands, with a named contact.

faq.q: How much time should we allow?
faq.a: A typical review takes one to two weeks. A larger site may need longer, so we confirm timing when we agree the scope.

faq.q: What access does the audit require?
faq.a: Read access to Analytics and Search Console usually covers the data review. Hosting credentials are unnecessary for the audit.

faq.q: Can our own developers carry out the work?
faq.a: Yes. The recommendations are designed for handover, and implementation support can be scoped separately.

deliverables: Technical, content and link findings backed by examples.
A comparison with competing sites and an ordered list of fixes.
Written report and a call or recorded walkthrough.

faq.q: Which platforms do you support?
faq.a: The team works on WordPress, Shopify and custom sites. Platform-specific checks can include theme performance, plugins and caching.

faq.q: Can our developer implement the fixes?
faq.a: Yes. We can write the tickets, discuss the changes and test the result after deployment.

faq.q: Can the scope cover multilingual websites?
faq.a: Yes. International projects can include language targeting and hreflang review when that is relevant to the site.

deliverables: Crawl findings and development tickets ordered by impact.
Redirect mapping and pre-launch checks for a migration.
A verification crawl, with post-launch monitoring for migrations.

faq.q: How do you handle several locations?
faq.a: Each branch is reviewed separately, including its business profile, directory records and local page. A combined report lets you compare locations.

faq.q: How do you quote the work?
faq.a: The team discusses branch count and scope on a discovery call before proposing a fixed monthly fee.

faq.q: Can we begin without a website?
faq.a: We can start by planning a basic local page that gives people a destination from your business profile.

deliverables: Business Profile and listings review for each agreed branch.
Local page plan and a process for requesting genuine customer reviews.
A shared report covering local calls, directions and map visibility.

faq.q: Who owns the completed work?
faq.a: Your company owns the paid-for articles and associated files.

faq.q: How do you handle specialist topics?
faq.a: A writer interviews your subject expert and asks them to review the draft. Editorial review and fact-checking are part of the process.

faq.q: Are Urdu and Roman Urdu available?
faq.a: English is the main publishing language. Urdu or Roman Urdu pieces can be discussed for the specific audience and brief.

deliverables: Topic plan and approved briefs aligned with your services.
Edited articles or landing pages with specialist review where needed.
Refresh and distribution plan for existing material.

faq.q: Do we keep our profiles and advertising accounts?
faq.a: Yes. Your team owns them and grants the working permissions needed to manage the agreed channels.

faq.q: How are advertising costs paid?
faq.a: You pay the advertising platform directly. The management fee covers the agreed planning, creative and campaign work.

faq.q: Can we use English and Roman Urdu together?
faq.a: Yes. Publishing language follows your brand and the way customers use the channel.

deliverables: Monthly content calendar submitted for approval.
Channel-specific copy, visuals and short video as scoped.
Campaign report showing leads, costs and the next tests.

faq.q: How long is the initial engagement?
faq.a: The stated starting term is three months for setup and testing. It then continues monthly.

faq.q: Can our internal marketing lead stay involved?
faq.a: Yes. Scope the tasks retained in-house and the specialist tasks assigned to Cloud Haven, with a shared performance report.

faq.q: Who owns the campaign assets?
faq.a: The client retains the accounts and content. The team works with delegated access, and platform spend is billed separately from the agency fee.

deliverables: Launch — basic SEO, two social channels, two content pieces a month and a quarterly review call.
Grow — full SEO, three social channels, one ad platform, four monthly content pieces, email and a quarterly landing page.
Scale — multi-market SEO, Google and Meta campaign management, tailored content and fortnightly review calls.

faq.q: Is the service intended for Pakistani or US providers?
faq.a: The main client group is US practices. A Pakistani provider can enquire and the team will assess whether the service fits its needs.

faq.q: How are the fees structured?
faq.a: A per-claim arrangement or a percentage of collections may suit the work. Claim volume and payer mix inform the written proposal.

faq.q: How does a new engagement begin?
faq.a: The team favours a short pilot so both sides can evaluate the workflow before confirming a wider agreement.

deliverables: Sample billing and receivables review to agree the starting point.
Pilot workflow inside your billing system where compatible.
Monthly collections, denial and receivables report with action items.

faq.q: Will we need to change billing systems?
faq.a: Where compatible, the billing team works through access your practice grants in its existing system. The fit is discussed at discovery.

faq.q: When are review calls scheduled?
faq.a: Coverage and calls are agreed around the practice’s hours. The team documents the schedule before launch.

faq.q: What should we review before sharing patient data?
faq.a: Discuss access controls, current security documentation and business associate agreement arrangements directly with the team during scoping.

deliverables: Discovery around specialty, payers, systems and working hours.
An agreed workflow and a limited batch of claims for the pilot.
Monthly review call and written action list for the practice.

faq.q: Can we outsource one stage first?
faq.a: Yes. Some practices start with claims or accounts receivable and add denial management or front-desk checks later.

faq.q: Which indicators will we see?
faq.a: Typical measures include days in receivables, clean-claim and denial rates, and collection trends. The practice and team agree on the final set.

faq.q: How does revenue cycle work extend beyond billing?
faq.a: It can cover eligibility and registration before a claim, then reconciliation, follow-up and management reporting afterwards.

deliverables: Baseline review and a written allocation of responsibilities.
Open balances and denials worklists for agreed stages.
Performance report using the measures agreed before launch.

faq.q: Can we keep patient contact in-house?
faq.a: Yes. In a hybrid model the practice can retain front-desk and patient-facing work while the partner handles agreed back-office queues.

faq.q: How do we decide whether to expand a pilot?
faq.a: Compare its performance against the starting measures and agree what needs to change before adding more stages.

faq.q: What happens if we end the arrangement?
faq.a: Notice and data-return terms are discussed before signature, so both sides know how to hand the work back.

deliverables: A written split of duties between practice and partner.
A limited pilot with turnaround measures and a baseline.
A handover plan covering ongoing access, notice and data return.

faq.q: Can you take over older denied claims?
faq.a: The first review checks each claim’s age against the relevant payer deadline. That determines which responses remain available.

faq.q: What happens when clinical judgement is needed?
faq.a: We prepare the paperwork. The provider reviews the clinical argument, particularly for medical necessity appeals.

faq.q: How can we see which items are open?
faq.a: A shared status log records each denial, and monthly reporting summarises open appeals, trends and recoveries.

deliverables: Prioritised denial log with an owner and appeal deadline.
Corrected claims or appeal drafts with supporting records.
Recurring-cause analysis and specific feedback for practice teams.

faq.q: Who decides whether treatment is clinically appropriate?
faq.a: Your provider makes the clinical decision. Our role is to check payer requirements, prepare paperwork and track the request.

faq.q: What happens after an unfavourable decision?
faq.a: We record the payer’s reason and prepare the appropriate correction or appeal for the provider to review.

faq.q: Which insurers can be included?
faq.a: During onboarding the practice and team confirm which payers it bills and which approval workflows are in scope.

deliverables: Requirements and evidence checklist by payer and service.
Submission references and a shared authorisation status log.
Expiry reminders, renewal tracking and turnaround reporting.

faq.q: How long does payer enrolment take?
faq.a: It varies by payer and file. Several weeks to a few months is common, and the payer controls the final decision.

faq.q: Can a group practice use one tracker?
faq.a: Yes. Tasks are organised by provider and payer and brought together in a shared tracker.

faq.q: What is the CAQH profile used for?
faq.a: Many payers use it to review provider information. Maintenance includes checking details, updating documents and tracking re-attestation dates.

deliverables: Provider document checklist and application package.
A shared status tracker for providers, locations and payers.
CAQH maintenance, re-attestation reminders and renewal calendar.

faq.q: Can you help carry out the plan?
faq.a: Yes. Implementation support can follow the assessment so the people doing the work have help with processes, tools and training.

faq.q: Can a founder based abroad use the service?
faq.a: Yes. Meetings and progress reviews can happen remotely. Legal filings, tax or audit work are coordinated with the appropriate licensed professionals.

faq.q: How is a project priced?
faq.a: After the free initial conversation, you receive the proposed scope and fee in writing.

deliverables: Diagnostic project — a two-to-four-week review ending with written findings and an owned action plan.
Monthly advisory — scheduled planning sessions, KPI reviews and support between meetings.
Implementation support — process or tool setup, staff training and handover documents.

faq.q: Do you take shares for the work?
faq.a: The advisory engagement is fee-based. The founder retains their equity.

faq.q: What help is available before a fundraising conversation?
faq.a: The team can prepare a pitch deck and financial model and help rehearse investor questions. Funding and introductions depend on others.

faq.q: Who completes legal and tax filings?
faq.a: The team helps plan registration and coordinates with licensed professionals who handle the formal filings. You retain ownership of the accounts.

deliverables: Validation findings, pricing assumptions and a decision on the next test.
Business plan, budget, financial model or pitch materials as scoped.
An example 90-day launch roadmap tailored to the venture.

faq.q: Which size of company usually seeks this support?
faq.a: The firm describes its typical engagement as a company of roughly 15 to 300 people. A smaller team can discuss a lighter assessment.

faq.q: Will we need a new reporting platform?
faq.a: The starting point is often an existing tool such as Excel, Google Sheets or Looker Studio. Tool selection follows the reporting need.

faq.q: How will we know whether the changes help?
faq.a: Before work starts, we agree measures such as decision time, how often issues reach the owner and whether monthly reports arrive on schedule.

deliverables: Role definitions and a map of decision responsibilities.
KPI dashboard or management report using existing tools where practical.
A meeting schedule and review process agreed with leadership.

faq.q: How long is a single workflow project?
faq.a: Four to eight weeks is typical. Larger programmes can be divided into separately reviewed phases.

faq.q: Which measures suit a pilot?
faq.a: Choose two or three before making a change. Turnaround time, repeat errors and staff hours are examples that can be checked again afterwards.

faq.q: Can we use the software we already have?
faq.a: Yes. The team starts with existing tools and considers an additional system only where the expected benefit justifies it.

deliverables: A map of a real workflow, including delay and rework.
A tested change, written procedure and handover to staff.
A review of agreed measures after 30 and 90 days.
